page: Amazon Web Services inf1.6xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, targeted at deep learning inference workloads. The host platform is powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor offering 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system configuration includes 48.0 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by four integrated AWS Inferentia ASICs with a combined 32 GB of accelerator memory. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no onboard local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for all persistent filesystem requirements.

Benchmarking data reveals top-quartile PassMark memory performance with a score of 2769.15, supported by uncached read bandwidth measuring 117.87 GB/sec. General CPU compute benchmarks position the server within mid-tier performance percentiles, registering a PassMark CPU score of 23788.28 and Geekbench multi-core score of 9635.0. In language model inference evaluations, the Inferentia hardware delivers 1141.9 prompt tokens per second and 167.36 generation tokens per second on 135M parameter models, alongside 36.03 prompt tokens per second and 12.65 generation tokens per second on 7B models. Benchmark metrics for 70B parameter models are unavailable, reflecting capacity limits inherent to the 32 GB accelerator memory pool.

The server provides qualitative cost efficiency for targeted machine learning deployments where specialized ASIC acceleration outperforms general CPU processing without the higher expense profile of full-scale enterprise GPUs. Tradeoffs include the total absence of integrated local storage and fixed accelerator memory bounds that prevent deployment of large-scale foundation models. Amazon Web Services inf1.6xlarge is best suited for small-to-medium parameter deep learning inference, natural language processing pipelines, computer vision serving, and real-time inference microservices.

The system is equipped with 24 vCPUs and 12 physical cores derived from an Intel Xeon 8275CL x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is powered by four AWS Inferentia ASICs delivering 32 GB of total accelerator memory. It features a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides no bundled local instance storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong PassMark memory throughput, while CPU compute and model inference metrics fall within mid-range percentiles, reaching 167.36 generation tokens per second on 135M parameter language models. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and custom ASICs provide efficient resource utilization for model deployment, making this instance best fitted for natural language processing, real-time computer vision inference, and machine learning microservices.
